newsitem.title: USA: EPA sets stricter standard for termite treatments.
newsitem.headline: EPA sets stricter standard for termite treatments.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency Friday announced stringent new standards for termite pesticides in an effort to reduce human exposure to the insect poison.

The EPA said it will require manufacturers to show that their products control termites for at least five years, or are substantially safer than products now on the market, and to comply with a new termite products labeling rule they must provide evidence supporting their claims.
The EPA also will require improvements in labels to help ensure that handling, storage and disposal of termite products meet the agency's safety standards.
The labeling rule caps five years of work among the industry, state officials and the EPA, the agency said.
All soil treatments for termites distributed or sold by manufacturers after October this year will have to have labels that meet the new standards.
The new labels will be required at the retail level after October 1999.
